Photograph: Timmie/Shutterstock Frances MaoThu 15 Oct 2026 16.19 BSTFirst published on Thu 15 Oct 2026 09.34 BSTShareFrom 2h ago15.17 BSTWes Streeting’s meeting with his US counterpart Peter Hegseth at the Pentagon later today will be his first since becoming Defence Secretary in July.

As my colleague Dan Sabbagh noted above – there are lots of issues on the agenda, Iran, Ukraine, and not least the growing US-Nato rift and Washington removing bombers from a UK air base earlier this month amid reports of a possible Iranian plot.
 
 
 Hegseth has also been heavily criticised for his annoucement that he is planning to livestream a public execution by military firing squad on December 3.
 
 
 Streeting was asked on the weekend’s political shows his thoughts on such barbarity. He steered clear of any personal criticism of Hegseth saying only that the UK does not support the death penalty, and as such did not support such an event.
 
 
 PM Andy Burnham has described Hegseth’s proposed event as “abhorrent”.

Read moreUPDATE: The US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of the Fort Hood killer Nidal Hasan. Trump had previously said he approved of his secretary’s plan but there has been so much backlash this week to Hegseth’s bloodlust including protest by former military chiefs.
 
 
 Trump’s retreated from the idea, saying just now: “many very good and well meaing people would rather not watch him die.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting is due to meet his US counterpart Peter Hegseth at the Pentagon; Ukraine’s ‘betrayal’ by the Trump administration is a key issue as the UK has pledged to help faciliate reconciliation between Zelenskyy and Trump

Nigel Farage says you can’t vet everyone as several Reform politicians were caught on camera making racist, violent remarks about Black, Asian and Muslim people. He’s had to push back a party announcement as he scrambes with the fallout of the ITV exposure.

Labour has instructed its local council groups to end power-sharing arrangements with their Green partners if they don’t condemn the party’s new ‘Zionism is Racism’ policy. The Greens blasted this intervention into local politics as “undemocratic”.

And in a significant case, Jeffrey Donaldson, the ex-DUP leader, has been sentenced today to 15 years in prison for child sexual abuse crimes against two women when they were minors. The judge said the former party leader, who’d reached the “very height of public office”, had shown not a shred of remorse or shame or regret for his crimes and “it is only through the courage, resourcefulness and determination of two young women that you’ve been brought to justice”.

Prosecutors said “this case shows that sexual abuse can be hidden behind a facade of respectability” but that “no individual, irrespective of their position, status or public reputation, is beyond the reach of the law.”

Thanks very much for reading the blog today and feel free to get in touch with me or Andrew, who’s back next week.

Updated at 16.22 BST2h ago15.58 BSTReform councillors caught on video show racism 'systemic' in party - Muslim Council of BritainBen QuinnA new undercover investigation which recorded Reform UK councillors and election candidates making graphic threats of extreme violence and expressing racist and misogynistic views “exposes a rotten core of racism and Islamophobia” within the ranks of Nigel Farage’s party, according to the Muslim Council of Britain.

Britain’s largest Muslim umbrella body was reacting after ITV News broadcast the first parts of a year- long investigation into Reform UK, which has led to a number of councillors standing down from the party and Nigel Farage postponing what was to be a major policy announcement today.
 
 
 Dr Wajid Akhter, Secretary General for the Muslim Council of Britain told The Guardian:

double quotation mark“To hear elected officials casually use dehumanising language, advocate for the mass deportation of British citizens, and discuss hiding their true agenda should ring alarm bells for every citizen committed to a tolerant and democratic society.
  
  
  Islamophobia and racism are not isolated incidents within the party; they are systemic issues that continue to manifest despite repeated promises by the party leadership to clean house.

Condemnations and rushed resignations after being caught on camera are no longer enough. The leadership of Reform UK must take full responsibility for the culture of hatred that they have allowed to fester and mainstream within their organisation.
  
  
  Finally, it is telling that one of those exposed is a Solihull councillor and former Conservative. On promoting anti-Muslim hatred, there is a common thread from the Conservative Party normalising Islamophobia whilst in Government, to Restore, Reform and black-clad vigilantes intimidating innocent people on our streets today”.

2h ago15.54 BSTHalf of surveyed Scots think SNP 'incompetent' as conference beginsThese YouGov poll results will be pored over given the SNP conference is kicking off today – and PM Andy Burnham is due in town tomorrow.

The poll’s results have 50% of those surveyed saying the Scottish National Party is “incompetent”, while 51% called it “untrustworthy”.

The poll shows First Minister John Swinney’s personal approval rating is down to 34% and 53% are unfavourable to him.

The only party leader with a positive approval rating – across the UK not just in Scotland – is the prime minister. Burnham has an approval rating of 47% favourable, and 38% unfavourable.
 
 
 Reform UK’s Nigel Farage has the lowest favourability rating among Scots. 74% viewed him unfavourably, including 61% who are “very unfavourable” towards him, while only 18% regarded him favourably.

2h ago15.25 BSTStudents need to learn how to better articulate in age of AI - Education SecRichard AdamsThe Guardian’s Education editor Richard Adams has this dispatch on the government’s plans to help school students improve their speaking ability amid the influx of AI tools.
 
 
 Saying that “practical skills are disappearing from practical subjects,” education secretary Lucy Powell told school leaders that the arrival of AI would mean changes in what is being taught in England’s schools.

Powell said she wanted to expand on plans to give oracy - the skilled use of spoken language - the same status as literacy in classrooms, following the government’s recent curriculum review that recommended an oracy framework to match the existing frameworks for reading and writing used by schools.
 
 
 Powell told an education conference in Birmingham:

double quotation mark“With AI on the rise, we need to go harder on the skills that makes us human, like oracy.

“That ability to articulate yourself confidently is central to success in work and in life, but for too long it’s been a marker of privilege. Now it will become the right of every child - nobody left out because they can’t speak up.”

Paul Whiteman, the general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers, welcomed the emphasis on practical skills including oracy but said time would need to be made available.

double quotation mark“It is crucial that the ongoing review of the curriculum reduces other content in order to genuinely create the space to embed these skills, however. Teachers are already unable to cover the current curriculum in the time available.”

Updated at 15.44 BST3h ago14.58 BSTGreens says Labour threat to end council deals over Zionism motion is 'undemocratic'I reported earlier that the Labour party has instructed all of its councils in power-sharing deals with the Green Party to end the coalition arrangment if their Green counterparts do not condemn the ‘Zionism Is Racism’ motion passed at the Green conference 11 days ago.

There are 18 such councils in the UK potentially affected. Labour has asked each council group to write to their Green partners for “reassurances” that they condemn the policy, which PM Burnham called antisemitic.

If they don’t, Labour’s head office says the local Labour groups should end the power-sharing agreements.

The Green Party has responded saying such moves are “undemocratic”.

double quotation mark“For the Labour Government to conflate criticism of Israel with antisemitism is disappointing and wrong.

double quotation mark“Trying to tell local parties what to do and who they can work with is undemocratic.

double quotation mark“Whilst Labour continue to try to meddle in our internal democracy, arm a genocide and lock up protesting pensioners, we will not take lectures from them.”

The ultimatum will impact 17 councils across England and one in Wales, according to Labour. These are:

Derbyshire Dales (Lib Dem-led coalition)

Broadland (Lib Dem-led coalition)

West Suffolk (Labour-led coalition)

Rother (Coalition led by local independent group)

Runnymede (Coalition with Lib Dems, Greens and local independent group)

West Oxfordshire (Lib Dem-led coalition)

West Sussex (Lib Dem-led coalition)

North Somerset (Lib Dem-led coalition)

West Devon (Independent-led coalition)

Monmouthshire (Labour minority-led coalition)

Coventry (Labour-led confidence and supply agreement with the Greens)
